nodes.summary: For points $a = (a_1, a_2)$ and $b = (b_1, b_2)$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$, the aspect ratio of the axis-aligned rectangle with opposite corners $a$ and $b$ is $|a_1 - b_1| / |a_2 - b_2|$, the ratio of its horizontal side length to its vertical side length; it is $0$ when $a_2 = b_2$.
nodes.title: Aspect ratio

nodes.summary: For points $a = (a_1, a_2)$ and $b = (b_1, b_2)$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$, the axis-aligned (possibly degenerate) rectangle with opposite corners $a$ and $b$ is the list of its four vertices $(a_1, a_2)$, $(b_1, a_2)$, $(b_1, b_2)$, $(a_1, b_2)$, in this order.
nodes.title: Axis-aligned rectangle

nodes.summary: Let $\gamma$ be a map from the unit circle to $\mathbb{R}^2$. For points $a, b \in \mathbb{R}^2$ and an angle $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$, the rotated rectangle given by $a$, $b$ and $\theta$ is inscribed in $\gamma$ when its four vertices are pairwise distinct and each lies in the image of $\gamma$.
nodes.title: Inscribed rectangle

nodes.summary: For $z, w \in \mathbb{C}$ and an angle $\theta$, $R(z, w, \theta)$ is the list of four points $z e^{i\theta}$, $(\operatorname{Re} w + i \operatorname{Im} z) e^{i\theta}$, $w e^{i\theta}$, $(\operatorname{Re} z + i \operatorname{Im} w) e^{i\theta}$: the vertices, in order, of the axis-parallel rectangle with opposite corners $z$ and $w$, rotated about the origin by $\theta$. The rectangle is degenerate when $z$ and…
nodes.title: Rotated rectangle with given opposite corners

nodes.summary: For points $a, b \in \mathbb{R}^2$ and an angle $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$, the rotated rectangle given by $a$, $b$ and $\theta$ is the list of four points obtained by applying the rotation $(x, y) \mapsto (x \cos\theta + y \sin\theta, -x \sin\theta + y \cos\theta)$ about the origin to each vertex, in order, of the axis-aligned rectangle with opposite corners $a$ and $b$.
nodes.title: Rotated rectangle

nodes.summary: Let $\gamma : S^1 \to \mathbb{C}$ be a $C^\infty$ embedding of the unit circle (a smooth Jordan curve in the plane). For $z, w \in \mathbb{C}$ and an angle $\theta$, write $R(z, w, \theta)$ for the list of the four points $z e^{i\theta}$, $(\operatorname{Re} w + i \operatorname{Im} z) e^{i\theta}$, $w e^{i\theta}$, $(\operatorname{Re} z + i \operatorname{Im} w) e^{i\theta}$, in this order: the vertices of the…
nodes.title: Rectangular peg theorem (Greene–Lobb)

nodes.summary: Let $\gamma$ be a smooth Jordan curve, that is, a map from the unit circle to $\mathbb{R}^2$ that is a $C^\infty$ immersion and a topological embedding, and let $X$ be the set of all $r \in [0, 1]$ such that some rectangle inscribed in $\gamma$ has aspect ratio $\tan(r\pi/4)$. Then the Lebesgue measure of $X$ is at least $1/3$.
nodes.title: Hugelmeyer's theorem on aspect ratios of inscribed rectangles

nodes.summary: For a map $\gamma$ from the unit circle to $\mathbb{R}^2$, let $X(\gamma)$ be the set of all $r \in [0, 1]$ for which there are points $a, b \in \mathbb{R}^2$ and an angle $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$ such that the rotated rectangle given by $a$, $b$ and $\theta$ is inscribed in $\gamma$ and the axis-aligned rectangle with opposite corners $a$ and $b$ has aspect ratio $\tan(r\pi/4)$.
nodes.title: Aspect-ratio parameters of inscribed rectangles

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
